# Testing jballs on Windows 7

`win7` is a small shell script (`~/.local/bin/win7`) that builds this project
for Windows 7 and runs it in a QEMU virtual machine. It exists because jballs
is a Swing app and "it works on my Linux JDK 25" says nothing about how it
behaves on the oldest Java a real user might still have.

The point of the design is that the edit → test loop stays one command:

```sh
win7 export
```

That recompiles the project, jars it, and pushes the jar into the **already
running** VM. No reboot, no drag-and-drop, no shared folder.

---

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `win7 install` | First boot only — boots the Windows ISO to install the OS |
| `win7 start` | Boot the installed VM |
| `win7 stop` | Graceful ACPI shutdown (waits up to 60s) |
| `win7 status` | Running or not, disk usage, what's on the share disc |
| `win7 export [dir]` | Compile → jar → rebuild disc → push into the running VM |
| `win7 snapshot <name>` | Save a qcow2 snapshot |
| `win7 restore <name>` | Roll back to a snapshot (VM must be stopped) |

Run with no argument and you get `status`.

### Environment overrides

| Variable | Default | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `WIN7_PROJECT` | `~/jballs` | Export a different project |
| `WIN7_MAIN` | auto-detected | Pick the main class when there's more than one |
| `WIN7_ISO` | `~/Downloads/Win7_Ult_SP1_English_x64.iso` | Installer image |

---

## The everyday loop

1. Edit code in Eclipse as usual.
2. `win7 export` on the Linux side.
3. In the VM, open the **WIN7SHARE** disc (drive `E:`) and double-click
   `run.bat`.

Windows notices the new disc on its own, so step 3 works immediately — you do
not need to restart the VM or even close the previous run.

---

## How `export` works

### 1. Find the main class

Every `.java` file under `src/` is scanned for a `public static void main(`.
The fully-qualified name is rebuilt from the file's `package` statement plus its
filename, so `src/jballs/Main.java` becomes `jballs.Main`.

If exactly one is found it's used. If several are found the script stops and
asks you to disambiguate:

```sh
WIN7_MAIN=jballs.display.SomeOtherDemo win7 export
```

### 2. Compile for Java 8

```sh
javac --release 8 -d <tmp> <all .java except module-info.java>
```

Two things matter here:

- **`--release 8`** — Windows 7 cannot run anything newer than Java 8. The host
  JDK 25 would emit class file version 69, which no Win7 JRE can load. `--release 8`
  emits version 52 *and* compiles against the Java 8 API, so you also find out
  at build time if you've used something that doesn't exist in 8.
- **`module-info.java` is skipped** — the module system doesn't exist in Java 8,
  and a plain classpath jar has no use for it. The module only declares
  `requires java.desktop`, which is on the classpath by default anyway.

Non-`.java` files sitting in the source tree are copied into the output too,
matching what Eclipse does, so resources still resolve at runtime.

### 3. Jar it

```sh
jar --create --file <share>/jballs.jar --main-class jballs.Main -C <tmp> .
```

The jar is named after the project directory. A `run.bat` is generated next to
it that calls `java -jar`, falling back to the Temurin install path if `java`
isn't on the guest's `PATH`.

### 4. Rebuild the disc and swap it in

The share directory is turned into an ISO with Joliet and Rock Ridge extensions
(so long, mixed-case filenames survive) and labelled `WIN7SHARE`:

```sh
xorriso -as mkisofs -J -R -V WIN7SHARE -o share.iso share/
```

Then, if the VM is running, the disc is swapped through QEMU's monitor socket:

```
change share /home/sb0rp/VMs/win7/share.iso
```

`share` is the block device id given to the CD-ROM drive in the QEMU command
line, which is what makes it addressable this way.

---

## Why a virtual CD, and not a shared folder

This is the part worth understanding, because it's the reason the loop is fast.

A CD-ROM is the only host→guest channel that Windows **re-reads the instant the
media changes**. Swapping the disc is a single monitor command and the guest
picks it up with no reboot, no service, and no driver.

The alternatives were all worse:

- **Samba / `-net user,smb=`** — needs a Samba install on the host, and this
  QEMU wasn't even built with SMB support.
- **A second virtual hard disk** — Windows caches it; the guest wouldn't see
  changes without a reboot or a hotplug dance.
- **A USB stick image** — same caching problem, plus Windows 7 has no xHCI
  driver in-box, so it would need EHCI and a re-plug cycle per export.

The trade-off is that the disc is read-only, so it's host→guest only. That's
fine for this workflow.

## The VM

Files live in `~/VMs/win7/`:

```
win7.qcow2     60G sparse disk
share/         staging dir — what ends up on the disc
share.iso      built from share/ by `export`
monitor.sock   QEMU monitor (how `export` swaps the disc)
win7.pid       pid of the running VM
qemu.log       QEMU stderr, if it fails to start
```

Windows is installed as user `sb0rp` with no password, and the product key was
skipped — it's on the 30-day evaluation clock. Enter a key in System Properties
if that matters.

### Hardware choices

Every device here was picked so Windows 7 has an **in-box driver** for it and
Setup runs without a driver disk:

| Flag | Why |
|---|---|
| `-machine pc` (i440fx) | PIIX IDE and UHCI are drivers Win7 ships |
| `-vga std` | Plain VGA. QXL was tried and reverted — see Limits |
| `-device intel-hda` + `hda-duplex` | Win7 has an HD Audio driver in-box; AC97 does not |
| `-device e1000` | In-box network driver |
| `-device usb-tablet` | Absolute pointer, so the mouse doesn't need grabbing |
| `-rtc base=localtime` | Windows expects the RTC in local time, not UTC |
| `-cpu host`, `-smp 2`, `-m 4096` | KVM acceleration, 2 cores, 4G |

Audio goes to the host through PipeWire (`-audiodev pipewire`).

## One-time setup

The share disc carries the installers, numbered in the order they must be run.
Each needs **Run as Administrator**, with a reboot after 1 and 2:

1. `1-install-sha2.bat` — Windows updates KB4490628 then KB4474419
2. `2-install-clipboard.bat` — VirtIO serial driver + SPICE agent restart
3. `3-install-r3dfox.bat` — a Firefox fork that still supports Win7
4. `4-install-qxl.bat` — re-runs spice-guest-tools now that SHA-2 works
5. `jre8-setup.msi` — Temurin JRE 8, what actually runs the jar

### The Windows 7 driver-signing trap

Worth writing down because it cost hours and gives no useful error.

Windows 7 SP1 as shipped **cannot validate SHA-2 code signatures**. Modern
drivers install cleanly, appear in Device Manager, and report `Status OK` with
`ConfigManagerErrorCode 0` — and then the kernel silently refuses to load them,
so their child devices never appear. Nothing anywhere says why.

This is why `spice-guest-tools` installs its agent service but none of its
drivers. The fix is KB4490628 (servicing stack) followed by KB4474419 (SHA-2
support), then a reboot, *then* install drivers.

Pre-trusting the publisher's certificate does **not** help — it isn't a trust
problem, it's a missing hash algorithm.

---

## Limits

Things that are not misconfiguration and cannot be fixed here:

- **No Aero.** Aero needs a WDDM driver. Windows 7 only ever gets the XDDM
  `qxl` driver — the WDDM builds (`qxldod`, `viogpudo`) start at Windows 8. Win7
  also has no software compositing fallback, so it's Windows 7 Basic or Classic.
- **No 3D acceleration.** `virtio-gpu-gl` has no Win7 driver.
- **No GPU passthrough.** This laptop has one GPU (Intel Iris Xe) and it drives
  the built-in display; passing it through would black out the host with no
  fallback. GVT-g was removed for Gen12+, and Intel ships no Win7 driver for
  Iris Xe regardless.
- **QXL was tried and reverted.** It made the guest display glitch — QXL expects
  a SPICE client, and driving it through QEMU's plain GTK window is the
  badly-tested path. It couldn't have enabled Aero anyway (see above).
- **Host↔guest clipboard does not work yet.** The plumbing is in place
  (`qemu-vdagent` on a virtio-serial port, agent running, port enumerated) but
  text doesn't cross. Unresolved.
- **IE8 can't load most sites** — Windows 7's TLS is too old. That's what
  r3dfox is for.

---

## Troubleshooting

**`win7 export` says "several main classes"**
Set `WIN7_MAIN` to the one you want.

**`win7 stop` says it's still running**
Windows is probably showing a "programs still need to close" prompt. Answer it
in the VM, or force it with the `kill` command the script prints.

**The jar won't start in the VM**
Open a Command Prompt on the disc and run `run.bat` from there so the error
stays on screen instead of the window closing.

**VM won't start**
`~/VMs/win7/qemu.log` has QEMU's stderr.

**Something broke in Windows**
`win7 snapshot ok` before risky changes, `win7 restore ok` to go back. Restore
needs the VM stopped.

---

## Host packages

Arch splits QEMU into many pieces and the base install has almost none of what
this needs:

```
qemu-system-x86        base emulator
qemu-ui-gtk            the window — without it there is NO display backend at all
qemu-img               qcow2 creation and snapshots
libisoburn             xorriso, to build the share disc
qemu-audio-pipewire    audio backend
```
